_comment: Committed format-version-1 (framed stream) vectors, carried across byte for byte from cas/internal/crypto/testdata/vectors.json when the format was extracted into this module: every dek_hex, plaintext_hex and ciphertext_hex is CAS's, unchanged, which is the point — the ciphertext CAS wrote still decrypts here, and that is what proves this is an extraction rather than a rewrite that happens to pass its own tests. Generated once each with a fixed DEK and salt (see docs/format.md, 'Test vectors'). TestVectors_MatchCommittedTestdata decrypts each entry's ciphertext_hex directly; it must never be regenerated by re-encrypting plaintext_hex, since the whole point is to catch a silent wire-format change. If a committed ciphertext stops decrypting, that is a real failure, not a vector to refresh. More than one vector is committed deliberately: a single small vector whose only frame is index 0 with final=true cannot distinguish several wire format changes (nonce/AAD index endianness, final-flag encoding, wire stride, the finality rule) from the correct format, because index 0 is all-zeros and final=true is the only branch it exercises. These vectors reflect the format as of CAS's fix round 2: every frame's AAD includes the stream's entire 25-byte header, not just a copy of the magic bytes.
